claim: A belief state (posterior over hidden states) is a sufficient statistic of history; a POMDP is an MDP over beliefs with a piecewise-linear convex value function.
agent_test: Compare an agent that carries a structured hypothesis-posterior table against one that carries raw history, at equal tokens, on hidden-state tasks.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Exact POMDP solving is intractable: the finite-horizon decision problem is PSPACE-complete and the MDP one is P-complete (Papadimitriou and Tsitsiklis 1987, read via Bernstein et al. 2002); infinite-horizon policy existence is undecidable (Madani et al., abstract read). Puterman and the 1987 paper themselves were still not opened.
agent_test: Not testable; justifies bounded search budgets.

claim: Value of information is built into the optimal belief-space policy: from a uniform belief the optimal tiger policy listens first and commits only when the belief is lopsided (about two net hearings).
agent_test: On Tiger-like evidence tasks, measure whether the agent gathers until a posterior threshold vs commits at once, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Point-based and sampling planners (PBVI, Perseus, SARSOP, POMCP, DESPOT) reach near-equal quality at 10-100x lower cost by planning on sampled beliefs only; e.g. Tag: Perseus -6.17, PBVI -9.18, QMDP -16.9.
agent_test: Sample few hypotheses (particles) instead of enumerating; test K=3,5,10 at equal tokens.

claim: Planner scores depend on implementation: the DESPOT authors could not reproduce published POMCP numbers; timings from different machines are not comparable.
agent_test: Report variance over seeds; do not trust single-run gains.

claim: Treating a partially observable problem as fully observable (QMDP, surface cue as state) loses value: QMDP -16.8 vs belief-based -6 to -9 on Tag.
agent_test: Run tasks with aliased observations; check the agent keeps competing hypotheses distinct.

claim: Recurrent memory gives no systematic benefit on fully observable tasks but helps when observations go missing; tuned plain recurrent model-free RL matches specialised POMDP methods (18 of 21 environments).
agent_test: Ablate memory length at equal tokens on MDP-like vs hidden-state tasks.

claim: Seed variance can create false differences: the same TRPO configuration in two 5-seed sets gave t=-9.09, p=0.0016.
agent_test: Use at least 20 seeds or items and paired tests when comparing arms.

claim: Chat LLMs do not explore reliably: GPT-4 with a basic prompt shows suffix failure in over 60% of replicates (T=500, N=20); only 1 of 32 prompt designs worked well (T=100 scan).
agent_test: Bandit-style test with and without a code-held summary, at equal tokens.

claim: An external sufficient-statistic summary (per-arm counts and means) beats raw history for in-context prompting (Gemini Flash MAB few-shot 50.2 vs 27.5 win-rate), but for fine-tuning raw history was better (65.6). Boundary: on SWE-bench Verified an LLM summary of history did not beat simply masking old observations (Qwen3-Coder 53.8 vs 54.8; summaries lengthened runs by 13-15%).
agent_test: Give the agent a code-maintained summary vs the transcript, at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs update beliefs poorly over multi-round interaction: most plateau after round 1; Bayesian assistant final accuracy 81% vs 36-58% for off-the-shelf LLMs and about 58% for humans; chain of thought, numeric formats and more rounds did not fix it.
agent_test: Multi-round preference or diagnosis task; compare free-text belief vs explicit numeric posterior.

claim: Fine-tuning on Bayesian teaching fixes much of the updating gap and transfers to other domains, but verbalised beliefs can disagree with behaviour (agreement under 50% in some models).
agent_test: Not testable without training; but check consistency of stated belief and action.

claim: Explicit belief plus expected-information-gain lookahead improves question asking: UoT +38.1% average success over direct prompting (5 datasets, 5 LLMs), beats Adapted-ToT by 12.4; OPEN beats LM-only in a user study. Absolute vs relative gain not stated. The 38.1% is a RELATIVE gain (rebuilt exactly for Llama3-70B: 46.6). At equal tokens GPT-4 UoT beat CoT-SC k=33 (48.1 vs 32.6 on 20Q, 63.2 vs 42.5 on troubleshooting); only n=3 runs.
agent_test: Replicate on 20-questions style tasks at equal tokens against ToT and self-consistency.

claim: A sound external verifier beats self-critique: Blocksworld GPT-4 generator 40%, LLM+LLM 55%, LLM+VAL 88% (100 instances, reopened). A weak LLM verifier is worse than none when its false-negative rate is high: Game of 24 standard 5%, LLM+LLM 3%, sound 36%; Mystery Blocksworld verifier rejects 97% of correct answers; a 99%-accurate CoT verifier still left a 6 point gap at 17x tokens.
agent_test: Compare self-check vs code or tool check at equal tokens.

claim: Using the LLM as world-model prior inside MCTS beats using it as policy alone on novel and compositional tasks (VirtualHome compositional seen 71.2 vs 47.0; UCT without prior 0.0), at much higher compute.
agent_test: Equal-token test: one deep chain vs search over sampled thoughts.

claim: Search helps only when the LLM can propose plausible actions: Mystery Blocksworld stays near 10-28% even with a verifier; LLM-MCTS wins where the model is simpler than the policy.
agent_test: Gate search on proposal quality; test on tasks of varying difficulty.

claim: Belief-State Engine preprint: an external Bayes posterior gave 38/40 vs 32/40 on Tiger (gpt-4o), but return CIs overlap and the 64-state attack graph showed no separation; a natural-language belief tracker acted identically to no belief. Without any stated threshold the posterior arm listened 1.45 times; the free-text-posterior ablation and RockSample were never run; BSE used 2.45x the LLM calls.
agent_test: Replicate with larger N; compare code-held posterior vs NL belief.

claim: Tru-POMDP: LLM hypotheses as particles with Bayesian filtering and belief-tree search beat ReAct, Reflexion and LLM-MCTS in hidden-object tasks; a flat hypothesis list was worse than a single hypothesis.
agent_test: Compare tree-structured vs flat hypothesis elicitation.

claim: Transformers trained on hidden-Markov data linearly encode the Bayes belief state (R2 0.95 on Mess3) and DPT behaves like posterior sampling; this is training-time evidence, not prompt-time.
agent_test: Not directly testable on a scaffold.

claim: Models can state structure but fail to act on it: CogEval GPT-4 0/30 on unseen-graph shortest path; BALROG best NetHack progress 1.5%; RAGEN Echo Trap collapse in 3 of 4 environments.
agent_test: Test agreement between stated plan and executed action.

claim: Compacting history into a learned belief helps agents (PABU 81.0% completion, 26.9% fewer steps) but is trained on benchmark trajectories, not zero-shot.
agent_test: Test pruned history vs full transcript at equal tokens.

claim: Scale improves the direction of belief updates (BCC vs log params r=0.906) and latent inference, but the gain does not reliably reach downstream prediction.
agent_test: Score inference and action separately.

claim: Apart from the single BSE Tiger preprint, no source measured a chat LLM on a classic POMDP against the optimal belief-MDP policy.
agent_test: Run Tiger and RockSample-small with an LLM against the exact optimal policy.

claim: Stated belief and chosen action disagree in untuned LLMs (under 50% alignment on flight recommendation); deriving the action from the stated belief with an external rule was more accurate than the LLM's direct choice. Qwen 2.5 did not improve after tuning.
agent_test: Ask for the posterior table first, then pick the action with a code or fixed rule; compare with direct action at equal tokens.

claim: Structured hypothesis generation beats unstructured: a flat one-shot set of hypotheses was worse than a single best guess, while a 3x3 tree of hypotheses with Bayesian filtering worked (Tru-POMDP). No sweep over K exists.
agent_test: Compare K=1, 3, 9 hypotheses generated as a tree vs a flat list at equal tokens on a diagnosis task.

claim: LLM summaries of history can lengthen agent runs (+13 to +15% turns) by hiding failure signals, so they do not reliably beat plain observation masking on code tasks.
agent_test: Compare masking, summary and structured table on a debugging benchmark, tracking turns to stop.

claim: Planner comparisons are sensitive to implementation and seeds: POMCP scores could not be reproduced by DESPOT's authors, and identical RL configurations differed at p=0.0016. LLM planner comparisons with N of 20 to 40 and one sampling seed cannot resolve gaps of a few points.
agent_test: Use at least 3 sampling seeds and N>=200 per arm, shared code.
